1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioner mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its LAC no.
130/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sube Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 15 specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi, was acquired.

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the interested person and is owner/bhumidhar in actual and physical possession of share of the land bearing Khasra no.39/14/2 (20), 17(416) and 24 (416)

sentences.text: The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

The ld. Counsel for the petitioner has taken the following grounds :
(i) It is stated that the LAC has failed to consider the surface of the entire acquired land of the petitioners is very much even and as good as the surface level of the land which is provided by the DDA for setting up of residential colonies and industrial complexes and the said land of the petitioners has a great potential value as a building site.
(ii) In the present award, Ld. LAC has determined the market value as per the police of the government of NCT of Delhi which came into effect from 01.04.2001 and hence the market value of the land under reference is basied on the said police, which was prevailing in the year 2001.
Though, the notification U/s 4 of the LA Act in the present case is dated 21.03.2003.
There should have been an appreciation/ escalation for the intervening period of 2 years approx. on the market value determined by the government.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled Rameshwar Solanki, AIR 1995 DEL 358 and that appreciation/escalation @ 12% p.a. on market value, the market value would have been much more that what has been awarded.

(iii) The Ld. LAC failed to consider the damages sustained by the petitioners as the acquisition has injuriously affected the earnings of the LAC no. 130/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sube Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 petitioners because the land of the petitioners is very fertile from agricultural point of view and the same was yielding 3 crops in a year, thereby,
generating handsome income to the petitioners amounting to Rs. 50,000/ per bigha per year.

entities.text: Sube Singh & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) The water level of the said land under reference is at a very upper level and water beneath the land is potable water.

(v) The Ld. LAC has not considered the topographcial advantages which the land of the petitioners enjoy such as land being situated hardly at a distance of 1 k.m. away from the Main Rohtak Road (N.H. 10) and adjoining Delhi Metro Workshop at Village Mundka, Delhi which is fully operational and as such has great potential value as a building site.

Beside this, all sorts of amenities like roads,
electricity, water, schools, Dispensary, Telephones, Post office, police station, etc. are available at hand and on account of all these facilities, the land prices in and around village Rani Khera have gone very high.
Ld. LAC has also failed to consider the existence of residential colonies namely Meer Vihar and Bhagya Vihar which are existing within the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

Therefore, the market value of this land should be fixed @ Rs. 5,000/ per sq. meter keeping in view the potential value of land as building site and its future use.

(viii) It is stated that the petitioners have more agricultural land adjoining the acquired land within the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi which has not been acquired and therefore, the petitioners have to suffer losses on ccount of severance of their acquired land from unacquired land left with the petitioners.
Therefore, the petitioners claim 20% of the compensation to be determined by this Court on account of severance charges ads the same has been allowed/ granted by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 18.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.
Notice under Section 9 and 10 of the Act were issued to the land owners/interested persons inviting their claims in respect of the land.

Pursuant to the notices, claims were filed by the affected persons claiming different value of their land and,
thereafter, the said award has been passed.

It is, inter alia, submitted that the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of construction of structure, which is placed without the sanction of law, and in terms of section 4 notification, there were no structure, tree, well on the said land.
The said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colony and can be used for agricultural purposes only.

The ld. LAC categorised the land into three categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the LAC no. 130/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sube Singh &
Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 15 fertility and user of land.

7.

It is submitted that the ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for the year 2001 - 2002, which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
The ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block B".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 57 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 3,40,000 per acre from the market value of "Block A"
category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 12,30,000 per acre,
and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for different categories of land besides other statutory benefits.
It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.
20.

In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
21. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
LAC no. 130/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sube Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no.
14 of 15 RELIEF 22.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).

(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
